issue.title: CSV export fails on Windows when the output folder contains non-ASCII characters
issue.author: fixture-reporter

summary.text: The issue reports a Windows 11 CSV export failure in version 1.4.0 when the output folder path contains non-ASCII characters, producing a UnicodeEncodeError; exporting to an ASCII-only path works instead. A closely matching closed issue was found with the same symptom pattern, so this looks like a possible duplicate rather than a clearly distinct report.

known_facts.text: The reporter says CSV export fails on Windows 11 in version 1.4.0 when saving to a folder whose path contains a non-ASCII character (for example, `café`).
The reported error is `UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode character`, and saving the same table to `C:/Temp` succeeds.
There are no comments on the issue, so no additional clarification or workaround is documented in-thread.
The repository label catalog includes `bug`, `docs`, `enhancement`, `needs-info`, `question`, and `security`.
No issue template files were found in the repository's current default-branch `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE` directory, so there is no template-based reporting checklist to apply from the current branch.

missing_information: A maintainer may still want to confirm whether the failure occurs on other non-ASCII paths or only on accented folder names, but this is not required to recognize the symptom pattern already reported.
The issue does not mention whether the problem also happens on non-Windows platforms, but that absence does not block triage because the current report is already platform-specific.
content.draft_reply: Thanks for the report. This does look very similar to a previously reported Windows CSV export issue involving non-ASCII characters in the output path and the same `UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode character` message. Since saving to an ASCII-only folder works, this appears to be the same class of failure. I’m going to link this with the earlier report for tracking. If you have a chance, please confirm whether the problem also occurs with other non-ASCII folder names or only with accented paths like `café`.
limitations: I only reviewed the issue text, repository labels, and one closely related prior issue; I did not inspect source code or linked fixes.
The earlier similar issue was closed, but no patch or documented resolution was read, so I cannot confirm the underlying cause or whether this report is already fixed.
The repository's issue-template directory on the current default branch was empty, so there was no template guidance to check for missing required fields.

comparisons.reason: Both reports describe the same product area (CSV export), the same platform (Windows), the same non-ASCII path trigger, the same `UnicodeEncodeError` message, and the same workaround where exporting to `C:/Temp` succeeds. The target issue adds an explicit example path (`café`) and version 1.4.0, but those details are consistent with the older report rather than indicating a different failure.
similarities: Failure is triggered by a non-ASCII character in the output directory path.
The error text is the same `UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode character`.
Exporting to an ASCII-only path succeeds.
differences: The target issue gives an explicit example folder name (`café`) and states the reporter is on Windows 11 with version 1.4.0.
